# MM-P2-L2-HT02-S1 Lubrication and fluids - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-HT02

## Scope
This maintenance manual section defines lubrication and fluid handling controls for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02). It covers acceptable lubricants, transfer and storage practices, fill and service procedures, and recordkeeping required to support consistent quench and handling performance during heat treatment operations. This document applies to maintenance and process technicians responsible for EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and to quality personnel performing verification audits in accordance with QS-PROC-08 and the operating sequences referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Background and rationale: improper lubrication or contaminated fluids can compromise part geometry, surface finish, and metallurgical outcomes. Controls in this document are intended to prevent cross-contamination, ensure fluid integrity during service, and preserve the defined quench characteristics necessary for process repeatability.

Note: The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds.

The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376.

## Tools and materials
- Clean service cart or tray dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02.
- Filter-equipped transfer pump compatible with CFW-LUB-376.
- Closed-top, labeled containers for temporary holding that are dedicated to CFW-LUB-376.
- Particle and water-testing kits suitable for the lubricant formulation CFW-LUB-376.
- Personal protective equipment as required by site safety procedures and SOP-P2-L2-01.
- Clean, lint-free wipes and funnel with particulate screen.
- Seals and gasket kits approved for contact with CFW-LUB-376.
- Logbook or electronic record entry device for maintenance records, per QS-PROC-08.

All tools that contact lubricants or fluids must be cleaned and dedicated to EQ-P2-L2-HT02 or clearly marked for single-equipment use to prevent cross-contamination between lines.

## Procedure
Preparation
- Verify authorization: confirm maintenance task is authorized by the shift supervisor and documented per SOP-P2-L2-03.
- PPE and containment: don required PPE and place drip trays under service points to catch incidental spills.
- Identification: confirm lubricant to be used is the part number CFW-LUB-376. Only use containers labeled with CFW-LUB-376 and inspect seals prior to opening.

Fluid handling and transfer
- Inspect source container for integrity and verify labeling includes CFW-LUB-376. If label or seal is compromised, do not use and escalate per SOP-P2-L2-03.
- Use the dedicated, clean transfer pump fitted with a particle filter. Replace filter cartridges if they show visible loading prior to transfer to prevent particulate introduction.
- When topping or refilling systems, pour using a funnel with screen and collect runoff in the drip tray. Do not transfer lubricant via open buckets that are used elsewhere on site.

Service and component replacement rationale
- Replace seals and gaskets that contact lubricant whenever service access requires disassembly. Old seals can shed particles and introduce contaminants that affect quench performance.
- If any unexpected visual change in fluid appearance is observed during service, capture a sample for particle and water analysis using the testing kits provided. Document findings in the maintenance log.

Sample take and testing
- Collect lubricant samples after initial fill and following any event that could introduce contamination. Use clean sample bottles dedicated to CFW-LUB-376 and label with equipment id EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and the date of sampling.
- Perform particle count and water content analysis per the test kit instructions. If results exceed acceptable ranges as defined by the lubricant supplier documentation, remove the fluid from service and replace per the disposal and refill steps referenced in QS-PROC-08.

Quench and timing awareness
- Maintain awareness of process timing during service windows. The quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds. Any activity that could extend quench delay beyond this limit must be coordinated with production to avoid processing parts outside specified quench timing.

Cleaning and contamination control
- Clean all external surfaces of service points after completing work to prevent foreign material ingress.
- Dispose of used wipes, filters, and contaminated absorbents according to site waste procedures referenced in SOP-P2-L2-01.

Examples and common actions
- Example: during a seal replacement, collect a post-service sample and perform particle analysis. If particle levels are within supplier guidance, return the unit to service and note the action in the maintenance log. If not, schedule fluid replacement and notify quality per QS-PROC-08.
- Example: when topping to compensate for minor consumption, ensure label CFW-LUB-376 is confirmed and filter the top-up fluid inline to prevent introducing particulates.

Records to keep
- Maintenance log entry for each service action including date, technician initials, parts replaced (list part numbers used), and confirmation that CFW-LUB-376 was used.
- Sample analysis reports for lubricant quality checks identified during or after service.
- Incident reports for any event that may have affected quench timing, including actions taken to return the furnace to compliant operation.
- All records shall reference EQ-P2-L2-HT02 and be filed per QS-PROC-08.

## Acceptance criteria
- Lubricant in service at the conclusion of maintenance is confirmed to be the part number CFW-LUB-376 and is free of visible contamination.
- Post-service particle and water test results must indicate fluid condition acceptable for continued operation as determined by the lubricant supplier guidance and recorded in the maintenance log.
- No service activity results in a quench delay exceeding the quench delay maximum for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is 16 seconds. Any deviation must be reported and resolved before returning to normal production.
- Records for the service action, testing, and materials used are complete and filed in accordance with QS-PROC-08 and cross-referenced to SOP-P2-L2-01 and SOP-P2-L2-03.

Revision control and change management
- Any proposed changes to lubricant specification, handling methods, or acceptance criteria must be submitted through the site change control process and reference QS-PROC-08 for documentation requirements.

End of document.
